newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH OSCAR HOLDERS AIM AT BRITAIN'S RAF NEXT.
newsitem.headline: CZECH OSCAR HOLDERS AIM AT BRITAIN'S RAF NEXT.

text.p: The Czech film-making team of Zdenek and Jan Sverak, Oscar holders for the 1996 best foreign film "Kolya", have chosen an English-language yarn about Czechs serving in Britain's Royal Air Force for their next project.
The Czech daily Mlada Fronta Dnes quoted the son, the 32-year-old director Jan, as saying his father was working on a script for a World War Two story which would not be a "pure" comedy.
The title, cast and schedule are still a heavily-guarded secret.
The grey-bearded Zdenek is writing the script in Czech but it will be filmed in English, marking the successful pair's first attempt at an original English-language project.

The bittersweet "Kolya", about an old bachelor stuck with an abandoned Russian boy on the eve of Prague's 1989 Velvet Revolution, joined the Sveraks with film distributor Miramax, backers of the last year's Best Picture "The English Patient".

This time the Sverak team agreed with Miramax to try their hand at an English-language film which they said would open their quirky and touching work to a wider audience and maybe allow them a shot at a "Best Picture" Oscar.

The pair has made a splash globally with lower-budget "humanistic" films mixing personal stories with a tinge of politics -- such as the post-war boy's life tale "Elementary School" which was nominated for the 1992 Oscar but lost.
The new project may give them a chance for a few more visual effects.

"I really told my father not to limit himself to anything (with the new script)", Jan told Mlada Fronta Dnes adding that because the film would be in English, money for filming bombardment scenes might come easier.
